notes: Action to Control Cardiovascular Risk in Diabetes BP. Diabetes + high CV risk. Intensive BP: NO mortality benefit (8.8% vs 10.0% death, p=0.20). Reduced stroke 41% BUT increased adverse events. NEJM.
ACCORD Lipid trial. Diabetes + high CV risk. Fenofibrate: NO benefit on MACE (10.5% vs 11.3%, HR 0.92, p=0.32). Possible benefit in high TG + low HDL subgroup. NEJM.
ACCORD Glycemia trial. Diabetes + high CV risk. Intensive: INCREASED mortality (7.2% vs 5.7%, HR 1.22, p=0.04). STOPPED EARLY. Intensive glucose control harmful. Paradigm shift. NEJM.
Veterans Affairs Diabetes Trial. Type 2 diabetes. Intensive: NO CV benefit (26.4% vs 29.5% MACE, HR 0.88, p=0.14). Reduced A1c (6.9% vs 8.4%) without CV benefit. NEJM.

Action in Diabetes and Vascular disease: preterAx and diamicroN-MR Controlled Evaluation. Type 2 diabetes. Intensive: NO CV benefit (8.9% vs 9.6% MACE, HR 0.94, p=0.32). Reduced nephropathy 21%. NEJM.

Fenofibrate Intervention and Event Lowering in Diabetes. Type 2 diabetes. Fenofibrate: NO significant MACE reduction (13.7% vs 14.8%, HR 0.89, p=0.16). Reduced non-fatal MI 24%, improved microvascular outcomes. Lancet.

Bypass Angioplasty Revascularization Investigation 2 Diabetes. Stable CAD + diabetes. Early revasc: NO mortality benefit vs medical therapy (17.6% vs 18.2% death, p=0.70). Medical therapy acceptable in stable diabetic CAD. NEJM.

Intensified Multifactorial Intervention in Patients with Type 2 Diabetes and Microalbuminuria. Diabetes + microalbuminuria. Intensive: Reduced CV events 59% (30% vs 55%, HR 0.41). Reduced mortality 46%. Comprehensive risk factor control beneficial. NEJM.
